We remain positive on commodities in the medium-term, preferring gold over PGMs in the Precious Metals sector. We have also adjusted our short term ZARUSD weaker. ###### **Adjusting PGM price forecasts for lower growth outlook** The outlook for global growth has deteriorated significantly over the past three months. Our global Auto team has lowered its sales forecasts for 2011-2013E across all regions. Although operating conditions in South Africa remain challenging, low growth should see the platinum market remain in a fundamental surplus until 2013E. Investment demand should push the market into overall deficit in 2012-13E. By contrast we forecast the palladium market to be in modest surplus for 2011-12E, but only due to continued Russian stockpile sales. For FY11E and FY12E, we have lowered our platinum price forecast by 4% and 12%,our palladium price forecast by 11% and 30% and our rhodium price forecast by 11% and 38%. ###### **We continue to prefer Amplats over Impala** We believe Amplats has the greatest flexibility and number of options to weather the current difficult operating conditions in South Africa and the lower than expected demand for PGMs globally. Th

e stock is also more highly geared to a weaker Rand environment. Impala offers the highest dividend yield in the sector, at 4.1% FY12E, but benefits less from a weakening Rand. In addition, we believe Impala shares will be weighed down by continued uncertainty over Zimbabwean indigenisation plans. Of the mid-caps, we prefer Aquarius over Northam, Lonmin and RBPlat due to a more attractive valuation. We acknowledge that some of Aquarius’s underlying value will be seen as “at risk” given the Zimbabwean indigenisation process. However, in our assessment, this is already factored in. ###### **Revised valuation methodology; Risks to target prices** The sector is trading currently at 0.8x NAV, taking the 10-year average for the sector to 1.1x (previously 1.3x). To reflect this, we now apply a 1x NAV to our DCF-derived valuation for each stock. We also now apply a nominal WACC to cash flows driven by nominal commodity prices until 2017E and a real WACC thereafter. We retain our positive outlook on gold, which in turn is more supportive for platinum versus palladium and rhodium. The magnitude of our 2011F downgrades is c.11% for both rhodium and palladium given the lower investment demand support and a modest 4% for platinum. I

n Rand basket terms, we have upgraded our prices modestly by 0.5% as the weaker Rand forecast cushions some of the metal price downgrades. The downgrades in 2012F are more significant, with a 38% cut in rhodium, 30% cut in palladium and a 12% cut in platinum. The net result is a 13% downgrade to our Rand basket price. We expect rhodium to be lower in 2012F versus 2011F, but we still expect platinum and palladium prices to be higher in 2012F year on year. In line with our view that the low interest rate environment may extend into 2013, we have upgraded our gold price forecasts and in turn our platinum and palladium price forecasts modestly. We have introduced explicit forecasts for the period 2015 – 2017F before reverting to our long-term price by 2018F. Given our expectations that significant deficits emerge in both platinum and palladium, post the 2015 time horizon, our explicit forecasts are between 20 - 45% higher than our long-term price assumption. |**Figure 2: Deutsche Ba**

In our view, the miner has the greatest flexibility and number of options, compared with peers, to weather the current difficult operating conditions in South Africa and the lower than expected demand for PGMs globally. The company is coming to the end of its three-year restructuring plan in which it aimed to trim back production to match market demand, restructure its cost base, push for sustained improvements in productivity, and review its capital expenditure and capital allocation procedures. This process is largely complete, with a reasonable degree of success, in an extremely difficult operating environment. The next 12 months will likely see Amplats move onto the next chapter of its strategy, in our view – we expect management to focus on growing market share from the current 40%, through ramping up production to meet a projected 4% demand growth in platinum, ahead of production growth from peers. We believe the focus of growth will be on three sources of lower-grade, but lower-cost, ounces: Western Limb UG2, Moga

lakwena and Unki. In our view, capex will have to rise from the current levels of R8bn per year to achieve this (potentially up to R10bn per year to fund 4% production growth on a 10-15-year view), but employee productivity should also rise and cash operating costs per tonne should remain fairly steady in the face of tough inflation trends. Buy. 

###### **Next catalyst for the stock: 3Q11 production report should be positive overall** 

Amplats will report 3Q11 production statistics in late October (likely 20 October). Whilst we expect the company to report a continuation of the difficult operating environment, we believe Amplats will reiterate its guidance to refine and sell 2.6m ounces of platinum for the year to December 2011 which should be taken positively by the market. We do not expect the company’s Western Limb mines to have seen much improvement on 1H11, given a continued poor safety performance and the effect of the resultant production interruptions. Unki and Mogalakwena, by contrast, should see continued successful rampup in our view – these two mines are ramping up to 70kozpa and 350kzopa by mid-2012 and end-2015, and are Amplats’ two lowest cost mines. In the meantime, we expect Amplats to continue to struggle to contain unit costs below R12,500. Company guidance is for 2H11 cash operating costs per equivalent refined platinum ounce to average R12,000, bringing FY11 costs down to R12,400-12,600. Our forecasts are in line with this guidance. 

###### **Valuation; target price reduced 2% to R725** 

We value Amplats on a sum-of-the-parts DCF basis, applying a nominal WACC of 13% to cash flows from 2011E-2017E (based on nominal commodity prices) and a real WACC of 8% to cash flows from 2018E onwards (based on real commodity prices). 

###### **Risks** 

Downside risks to our price target include lower-than-forecast PGM metals prices; a stronger-than-forecast ZAR/USD exchange rate; a more negative-than-expected outcome in Zimbabwe regarding indigenisation; and higher-than-forecast capex to sustain higher production levels in the longer term (our base case assumes a peak of R12bn in 2014).
